title: grpc-streaming-throughput-degeneration-scratchpad-arpita
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad to capture experiments investigating throughput degeneration observed when using gRPC server-side streaming for multi-turn token streaming with continuous clients. Trying to reproduce the intermittent throughput collapse seen in staging traffic spikes.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Head-of-line blocking inside HTTP/2 connection when many long-lived streams coexist (max concurrent streams) causes throughput collapse.
- H2: Server-side backpressure + small per-message window leads to frequent context switches inside serving runtime, amplifying overhead and causing token emission stalls.
- H3: Inefficient batching path for streaming responses (fallback to unary-style emit) when payloads are small -> poor token-per-second efficiency.

Environment / baseline:
- Model: llama-like-13b-qat (quantized variant used in staging).
- Serving node: 1x A10G, 8 vCPU container, 40GB RAM, gRPC endpoint behind envoy (HTTP/2).
- Client: go-grpc client (v1.55), 64 concurrent connections simulated, each connection opens 8 streams (configurable). Total clients = 512 streams target.
- Workload: streaming generation, average token chunk = 32 tokens per message, 20 messages per request on average (multi-turn streaming), approx 640 tokens/request.
- Metric capture: server-side token-emitted-per-second, per-stream p50/p95 inter-message gap, envoy metrics (H2 stream counts), runtime CPU/threads, and client-side observed throughput.

Experiment 1: Vary max concurrent streams per HTTP/2 connection
- Configs: max_concurrent_streams = [16, 8, 4, 2, 1]. Keep total streams ~512 by changing number of clients accordingly.
- Observations:
  - 16: steady throughput ~48k tokens/s, p95 inter-message gap 60ms, stable CPU ~72%
  - 8: throughput ~45k tokens/s, occasional 500ms gaps (p95 250ms), small climb in envoy H2 stream queueing
  - 4: throughput drops to ~32k tokens/s, frequent 1–2s stalls on ~4% of streams, server thread wake contention observed
  - 2: severe drop to ~18k tokens/s, many streams starved; total active streams per connection saturating envoy queueing stats
  - 1 (1 stream per connection): throughput recovered to ~46k tokens/s but CPU cost increased due to many more TCP connections (conn count ~512)
- Quick take: lower concurrency per connection increases head-of-line sensitivity; a sweet spot exists (8–16) before connection management overhead dominates.

Experiment 2: Message chunk size (tokens/message)
- Configs: tokens/message = [8, 16, 32, 64, 128] (keep msg frequency adjusted so same aggregate tokens/request)
- Observations:
  - 8 tokens/msg: many small writes -> high syscalls; throughput ~30k tokens/s, p95 inter-message gap spiky
  - 16 tokens/msg: ~38k tokens/s, fewer spikes
  - 32 tokens/msg: best ~48k tokens/s
  - 64 tokens/msg: slight decline to ~44k tokens/s (bigger messages incur serialization + socket buffer behavior)
  - 128 tokens/msg: throughput ~36k tokens/s, larger tail latencies; memory copy overhead in runtime increases
- Quick take: medium-sized chunks (24–40 tokens) are optimal for our runtime+envoy path.

Experiment 3: Server-side emit path vs simulated unary fallback
- Approach: instrumented runtime to toggle streaming optimized path (continuous buffer + coalesced write) vs fallback path (per-token write w/ flush).
- Observations:
  - Streaming-optimized path: stable 48–52k tokens/s
  - Fallback per-token write: 12–16k tokens/s, significant CPU syscall overhead, created hotspots in runtime emitter thread
- Quick take: ensure streaming optimized path is used for >1 token per message; fallback should be disabled or only used for debug.

Experiment 4: Backpressure simulation (client read slowdown)
- Setup: 10% of clients intentionally sleep 250–2000ms between reads to simulate slow consumers.
- Observations:
  - With default per-connection queueing, slow consumers dragged entire connection; when many slow streams present, other fast streams on same connection saw increased latency (head-of-line).
  - Solution mitigations: smaller max_concurrent_streams per connection, per-stream prioritization (HTTP/2 weight) showed improvement but not complete fix.

Performance table (representative numbers):
Tokens/s | config
48,000   | max_streams=16, tokens/msg=32, optimized_stream_path
45,000   | max_streams=8, tokens/msg=32
32,000   | max_streams=4, tokens/msg=32
18,000   | max_streams=2, tokens/msg=32
46,000   | many connections (1 stream/conn), tokens/msg=32
12,000   | fallback per-token write, tokens/msg~1

Runtime traces / symptoms observed:
- Thread wake contention on emitter when many small writes
- Envoy H2 queued_streams increments when streams exceed ~50 per connection under load
- Kernel socket send buffer stalls visible for connections with mixed slow/fast streams

Immediate action items (TODOs):
- [ ] Add a guard in streaming path to coalesce small messages for N tokens or wait up to X ms before flush (tunable)
- [ ] Expose recommended client defaults: tokens/message ~= 24–40, disable per-token flush
- [ ] Experiment with HTTP/2 prioritization weights (in envoy) and measure improvement on mixed-speed clients
- [ ] Add metric: per-connection slow-stream fraction + per-stream stall time (to drive alerts)
- [ ] Verify gRPC libraries in other languages (python/node) behave similarly re: stream coalescing

Notes to self / debugging commands used:
- client runner: ./bin/stream-bench --clients=64 --streams-per-client=8 --model=llama-like-13b-qat --tokens-per-message=32 --messages=20
- tcpdump filter used: tcpdump -nni any port 443 and host <server-ip> -w dump.pcap
- envoy admin: /stats | grep queued_streams
- simple runtime trace: TRACE_EMIT=1 ./run_server (produces per-write timing log)

Longer-term ideas:
- Consider switching streaming transport to multiplexed single-shot websocket path for noisy multi-tenant traffic (requires tradeoffs with HTTP/2 ecosystem)
- Build a client-side helper lib that batches small messages before sending to avoid pathological small-chunk patterns in customers' apps

Open questions:
- How many real customers are using tokens/message < 20 in prod? query usage logs + correlate regressions with chunk size
- Is there a runtime-level lock we can remove or make shard-local to reduce emitter contention? (Marta to take a look at 1221 emitter patch)

References / links:
- Linear: RW-8342 (backpressure / streaming stalls)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1293 (initial streaming coalesce prototype)

Bottom line: gRPC streaming is performant when messages are medium-sized and connections carry multiple streams (8–16). Pathological slow consumers and many tiny writes trigger head-of-line and emitter contention that cause orders-of-magnitude throughput degeneration. Immediate mitigations are: coalescing small writes server-side, recommending client chunking defaults, and adjusting per-connection concurrency.

End of scratchpad.
